newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geberit says sales rose in 1997 first half.
newsitem.headline: Geberit says sales rose in 1997 first half.

text.p: Switzerland's Geberit Group, acquired in March by London-based private fund manager Doughty Hanson, said consolidated sales in the first half of 1997 rose 8.7 percent to 500.7 million Swiss francs.
Currency adjusted sales rose by 3.8 percent.

Its consolidated operating results before interest and taxes (EBIT) were 66.2 million Swiss francs, including about 22 million francs of goodwill amortisation and other intangible assets resulting from the acquisition. Operating cash flow was 112.8 million francs. It gave no comparative figures for 1996 first half EBIT or cash flow.
It said first-half sales in Germany, Belgium, Austria and Italy rose. Sales in France and the Netherlands were steady while Swiss sales fell five percent versus the previous year.
"In spite of the continuing building recession in the main European markets the Group Executive Board expects a positive business development also in the second half year," it said.
It said it was also stepping up its acquisitions and cooperations.
Geberit is one of Europe's leading suppliers of sanitary technology, including plumbing and bathroom fixtures.
The company said in March when it was sold by its private owners to Doughty Hanson that it planned to seek a bourse listing within three to five years. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
